# SSGOI setup guide

SSGOI adds native app-like page transitions for mobile web apps without
replacing the application router.

Router agnostic. Cross-browser. SSR ready. Web Animations API powered.

Current version: `@ssgoi/core@7.1.0-beta.2`. Every `@ssgoi/*` framework package
is released in lockstep with core, so install the same version across them.

This file contains the minimal Next.js App Router setup. The root React package
remains router agnostic. Read linked files only
when their topic applies.

React Native / Expo Router has a separate experimental source preview:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/expo.txt
The web setup and preset catalog below do not apply unchanged to native views.

## Choose a mobile interaction

Start with the UX relationship, then open the linked transition spec for props
and a focused example.

| UX | transition | route rule | spec |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| list → detail, drill deeper | `drill()` | `on` + `except` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/transitions/drill.txt |
| compose, filters, temporary task | `sheet()` | `on` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/transitions/sheet.txt |
| ordered tabs or steps | `slide()` | `ordered` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/transitions/slide.txt |
| card or image → detail | `zoom()` | `from` / `to` | https://ssgoi.dev/llms/transitions/zoom.txt |

Representative mobile config:

```ts
import { drill, sheet } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [
    // A detail route drills in; returning to the list drills out.
    {
      on: "/posts/**",
      except: "/posts",
      transition: drill(),
    },

    // A temporary task rises above the current page.
    {
      on: "/compose",
      transition: sheet({ type: "blur" }),
    },
  ],
};
```

For variants and more effects, open the transition catalog:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/transitions.txt

## Minimal Next.js App Router setup

### 1. Install

```bash
npm install @ssgoi/react
```

### 2. Provider and config

Keep one config and one `<Ssgoi>` above routed content:

```tsx
// app/ssgoi-provider.tsx
"use client";

import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Ssgoi } from "@ssgoi/react";
import { drill } from "@ssgoi/react/view-transitions";

const config = {
  transitions: [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill() }],
};

export function SsgoiProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <Ssgoi config={config}>{children}</Ssgoi>;
}
```

To select different rules for mobile and desktop:

```ts
transitions: ({ isMobile }) =>
  isMobile
    ? [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill() }]
    : [{ on: "/**", except: "/", transition: drill({ type: "slide" }) }],
```

### 3. Route boundary

Import the ready-made boundary. It reads the pathname and sets the key and
transition id together; it also handles URL-hook Suspense. No local boundary
file is needed:

```tsx
import { SsgoiRouteBoundary } from "@ssgoi/react/nextjs";

<SsgoiRouteBoundary>{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
```

### 4. Layout

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { type ReactNode } from "react";
import { SsgoiProvider } from "./ssgoi-provider";
import { SsgoiRouteBoundary } from "@ssgoi/react/nextjs";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <main className="relative z-0 min-h-dvh overflow-x-clip">
          <SsgoiProvider>
            <SsgoiRouteBoundary>{children}</SsgoiRouteBoundary>
          </SsgoiProvider>
        </main>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

The class string above is Tailwind shorthand. Without Tailwind, apply
`position: relative; z-index: 0; min-height: 100dvh; overflow-x: clip`. Use
`clip`, not `hidden`: `overflow-x: hidden` makes the wrapper the scroll
container, and scroll restore then targets the wrong element. Fall back to
`100vh` only where `dvh` is unsupported.

That is the complete simple setup. The `nextjs` entry is a subpath of
`@ssgoi/react`, not a separate package to install. Next.js is an optional peer;
installing or importing `@ssgoi/react` does not install or load it.

Next.js interception, redirects, and rewrites remain application routing
concerns. If your app uses middleware (Next 13–15) or proxy (Next 16+), keep its
matcher and rewrite/redirect rules compatible with both soft intercepted
navigation and direct page entry. The boundary does not configure these rules.
For background slots, resolve from `selectedSegments` rather than the modal URL.
Short setup and verification: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/complex-routing.txt

Other ready-made entries: `@ssgoi/react/react-router`,
`@ssgoi/react/tanstack-router`, `@ssgoi/svelte/sveltekit`,
`@ssgoi/vue/nuxt`, `@ssgoi/vue/vue-router`, `@ssgoi/solid/solidstart`.
Each router is an optional peer, external to the build, and only loaded by its
entry. Use the installed router's entry; do not install all the routers.
For a custom router or direct DOM control, use the manual guide:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/manual-boundaries.txt

Browser note: the listed compatibility target is for the core Web Animations
API runtime. `sheet({ type: "blur" })` and `zoom({ type: "blur" })` also use
`backdrop-filter` (Firefox 103+). Earlier Firefox keeps the transition, scale,
and dimming but omits the backdrop blur.

SSGOI also chooses scroll reset or restoration from the matched UX
relationship:

- `from` / `to` restores the forward source and resets the destination.
- `on` does the same when navigation crosses the scope boundary. Navigation
  between two paths already inside the same `on` scope treats both as semantic
  `to` and resets both by default. For stack UX, use `except` to keep the source
  outside the scope.
- `ordered` restores both sides.

Override one rule with `preserveScroll` only when the default does not fit.
Details: https://ssgoi.dev/llms/scroll-restoration.txt

Complete Next.js guide:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/frameworks/nextjs.txt

## Route rules in one minute

Transitions describe motion. Route rules describe the navigation relationship:

```ts
const config = {
  transitions: [
    // Entering the scope is forward; leaving is backward.
    { on: "/posts/**", except: "/posts", transition: drill() },

    // The written pair is forward; the reverse is backward.
    { from: "/gallery", to: "/photo/*", transition: zoom() },

    // Increasing index is forward; decreasing index is backward.
    {
      ordered: ["/tabs/home", "/tabs/search", "/tabs/profile"],
      transition: slide(),
    },
  ],
};
```

- `on` selects a route or route family.
- `except` removes paths from an `on` scope.
- `from` / `to` defines a precise pair, bidirectional by default. Set
  `bidirectional: false` for a one-way pair.
- `ordered` derives direction from path order.

Wildcards, arrays, priority, matching order, and mobile/desktop configs:
https://ssgoi.dev/llms/route-rules.txt
